interest: This document illustrates U.S. diplomatic monitoring of Japanese commercial and financial expansion into Central America during the mid-1930s. It records American diplomatic reporting on the rumored establishment of a Yokohama Specie Bank branch in San José, Costa Rica, reflecting U.S. concerns over Japanese economic penetration in Latin America prior to World War II. The sheet is also useful for researchers because it provides a direct cross-reference to State Department file 618.9411 (commercial relations between Costa Rica and Japan).
overview: This file consists of a State Department List of Papers index sheet for decimal file 894.51618, concerning Japanese branch banking in Costa Rica. It indexes a single despatch, Despatch No. 857 of September 18, 1935, sent from Costa Rica by American Minister Leo R. Sack to the Department of State. The recorded document reports on rumors regarding the potential establishment of a branch of the Japanese-owned Yokohama Specie Bank in San José, Costa Rica, and notes a cross-reference to decimal file 618.9411.

subfiles.summary: This single-page List of Papers covers decimal file 894.51618 regarding Japanese branch banking in Costa Rica. It registers Despatch No. 857 dated September 18, 1935, from U.S. Minister Leo R. Sack in Costa Rica to the Department of State. The despatch relays reports concerning the rumored establishment of a branch of the Japanese-owned Yokohama Specie Bank in San José, with a notation cross-referencing the matter to commercial file 618.9411.
